chunks.text: 44-year-old female, Homemaker, resident of Punggol, Singapore.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Good morning, Mr. Tan. I'm Dr. Lim, the anesthesiologist who'll be taking care of you during your surgery today. Let me go through some questions to make sure we're all set for your laparoscopic cholecystectomy. First, can you tell me about your medical history?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: Sure, doctor. I have high blood pressure, diabetes, and high cholesterol. Also, my BMI is 32, so I'm quite heavy. But I can still walk and do my daily things, though I get tired faster lah.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Thank you. Let's go through your medications. What are you currently taking?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: I take amlodipine 10mg every day for BP, metformin 500mg twice daily for sugar, and atorvastatin 20mg at night for cholesterol. Oh, and I stopped metoprolol 50mg daily two weeks ago, as per my doctor's advice.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Alright. Do you have any allergies to medications, especially antibiotics or anesthetics?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: Ah, yes! I had a bad rash from sulfa antibiotics before. My skin turned all red and itchy, so I avoid that now. But my records say 'no known allergies'? Must be a mistake lah.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Thank you for clarifying that. We'll make sure to note the sulfa allergy. Have you had any previous surgeries or anesthesia?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: No, this is my first surgery. But I did have a minor procedure for my diabetes check-up last year, just local anesthesia, no issues.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Good. Are you NPO? When was the last time you ate or drank anything?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: Yes, I stopped eating after 8pm last night. Only sipped some water for my morning meds, but that was hours ago.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Perfect. Any other concerns or questions about the anesthesia or surgery?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: Just worried about the pain after surgery. Will I be able to manage it with the medications I'm on?

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: We'll ensure your pain is well-controlled. You'll have a multimodal approach with different medications, and we'll coordinate with your surgeon. Any other questions?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: No, that's all. Thank you, doctor.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: You're welcome, Mr. Tan. We'll take good care of you. I'll review your chart and see you in the holding area soon.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: [08:00] induction propofol one hundred twenty milligrams

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: [08:05] tube in, grade one view

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: [08:10] peripheral IV placed, 20 gauge

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: [08:12] arterial line placed, 22 gauge

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: [08:15] administered 500 milliliters normal saline

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: [08:30] mean arterial pressure dropped to fifty-five, gave one milliliter of phenylephrine

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: [08:40] heart rate increased to one hundred twenty, gave two milligrams of labetalol

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Hi there, how are you feeling after the surgery?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: Eh, still a bit groggy, but okay lah. Got some pain here, you know?

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Can you rate the pain for me? On a scale of 0 to 10, where 0 is no pain and 10 is the worst?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: Maybe 4 or 5? Mostly around the tummy area, like where they made the cuts.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Any nausea or feeling like you might vomit? Sometimes the anesthesia can cause that.

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: A bit, yes. Not too bad, but my stomach feels funny. Like I want to throw up but can't.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Okay, we can give you something for that. How's your breathing? Any tightness or coughing?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: Breathing is okay, but my throat sore lah. Like someone put a tube there.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: That’s normal after intubation. Do you remember anything from the operation itself?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: Nope, nothing. One minute I was talking, next thing I know, I’m waking up here.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Good. Now, since you have high blood pressure and diabetes, any headaches, dizziness, or thirst?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: Thirsty, yes. But no spinning or headache. Blood sugar was okay before surgery, right?

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: We’ll check your blood sugar and blood pressure now. Rest is looking good, but let us know if anything worries you.

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: Okay, thanks. Just want to go home soon and eat proper food.
